item.title: Syria rules out troop deployment to Yemen, says military ties with Saudi could expand
item.description: Syria has clarified that it will not deploy troops to Yemen despite previous reports suggesting otherwise. A diplomatic source stated that military cooperation with Saudi Arabia is anticipated to deepen in the future. Saudi Arabia is currently facing tensions with the Houthi rebels and seeks military assistance from various allies. Syria and Saudi Arabia recently signed a defense cooperation agreement as ties between the countries strengthen.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Zelenskyy says Russia hit Ukrainian energy facility with North Korean KN-23 missiles
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Russia is using North Korean KN-23 missiles against Ukraine. He emphasized the need for stronger global sanctions against countries supplying military assistance. Zelenskyy noted a critical shortage of US-made Patriot missile interceptors affecting Ukraine's defense capabilities. Russia's intensified attacks are exacerbating the situation as winter approaches. Military cooperation between North Korea and Russia has significantly increased in recent months.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Brooklyn tenants faced a $120,000 claim after renting from a fake owner; court later dismissed it after a sale
item.description: In a perplexing turn of events, Deborah and Demetris Jones rented an apartment under the false pretense of ownership in Brooklyn. Legal complications followed as the courts ruled the original landlord could no longer enforce tenancy agreements after selling the property. A subsequent settlement with the new owner granted the tenants temporary residence, illuminating significant considerations for tenants during changes in property ownership.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Dundee manager fired over £21,360 pothole repairs wins £34,326 compensation
item.description: A Dundee transport manager who worked for a furniture company for over 24 years was dismissed after it questioned £21,360 in pothole repair bills. A tribunal found that the company had failed to investigate the matter fairly, overlooked findings that cleared him of wrongdoing and wrongly dismissed him. It ordered the company to pay him £34,326.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: North Carolina student wins $2M, thanks to gas pump glitch
item.description: Bram Dunehew, a college student, experienced a life-changing moment when a gas pump malfunction led him to purchase a $2 million Powerball ticket. While waiting for his receipt at a convenience store, he decided on a whim to join the lottery. Dunehew matched all five white balls during the Halloween night drawing.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Canadian landowners donated property worth more than C$2 million
item.description: In a remarkable partnership, Ducks Unlimited Canada has safeguarded over 1,100 acres in southern Quebec, thanks to more than C$2 million in funding from local landowners. This significant conservation effort is vital for maintaining ecological balance and biodiversity, while a newly opened 1.5-kilometre trail enhances public access to these precious habitats.

item.title: Wrexham Kop Stand Expansion: planners clear 7,750-seat upgrade; capacity tops 18,000
item.description: The planning authority has given Wrexham AFC the go-ahead to increase the capacity of the new Kop Stand to 7,750 seats, enhancing the Racecourse Ground's venue status for major global events, such as international football. Work began on the stand in December 2025 and is set for completion by early 2027.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Woman’s niece discovers 1930 painting hidden for decades in New York apartment; artwork bought for $3,800 could fetch $3 million at auction
item.description: Georgia O’Keeffe’s long-lost artwork, 'Near Abiquiu, New Mexico I', is set to make waves at an upcoming auction. After nearly 40 years hidden in a New York apartment closet, the painting resurfaced thanks to a spontaneous mention by the niece of its original owner. It will be showcased to the public before its auction on November 17, 2026, with proceeds aimed at supporting family projects and educational initiatives.

item.title: Idaho hunters kill 12 newborn wolf pups in a single day
item.description: Three hunters in Idaho killed 12 wolf pups, receiving up to $2,000 for each animal. The state’s programme reimburses hunters, raising concerns over the use of taxpayer money. Critics have condemned these actions as a form of bounty hunting, especially targeting newborn pups. Wildlife experts have expressed concerns about the method of killings and potential effects on wolf populations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Cyndi Lauper, Ariana DeBose help New York charity gala raise over $750,000 for nonprofits
item.description: At the 2026 Fetch Pet Gala in New York City, stars like Cyndi Lauper and Ariana DeBose brought their talents to the stage, raising over $750,000 for four animal rescue nonprofits. This event also featured adoptable dogs gracing a green carpet, enhancing their chances for adoption. SATELLAI, the event's sponsor, contributed by providing devices to new pet adopters, showcasing a powerful community commitment to animal welfare through celebrity support.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Tiger Woods' former mistress Rachel Uchitel spends $100,000 on cosmetic surgery makeover
item.description: Rachel Uchitel, who made headlines in 2009 after being linked to golfer Tiger Woods, has reportedly spent $100,000 on cosmetic surgery. The 51-year-old podcast host underwent a facelift, brow lift and other procedures after years of facial fillers and aesthetic treatments left her unhappy with her appearance. She says she wanted a fresher, more natural look.

item.title: Nazi spies landed on US soil days before German U-boat sank Canadian ship off Maine in 1944; 82 years later, divers find wreck 400 feet underwater
item.description: Divers from the Nomad Exploration Team located the wreck of the SS Cornwallis nearly 400 feet underwater. This ship was torpedoed by a German submarine in December 1944, resulting in the deaths of 43 crew members. The submarine also secretly landed two Nazi spies on the coast of Maine just days before. The discovery highlights an important historical event involving espionage during World War II.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UK bride dances with hospitalised dad: she brings wedding to his ward; staff help arrange the dance
item.description: Sinead Jackson's wedding was uniquely touched by bittersweet circumstances as her father, Leslie Healy, was hospitalized only days before the event. Hospital personnel facilitated a heartwarming moment, allowing Sinead to don her wedding dress for a dance with her father. Though Leslie couldn't physically attend, technology enabled him to witness the ceremony.
